memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: "He must increase, but I must decrease." — John 3:30

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
There is a profound paradox in the Kingdom of God: the way up is down. We often spend our lives trying to build our "stature" our reputation, our influence, and our ego. Yet, the biblical path to true greatness begins with a deliberate shrinking of the self.
Bible mentioned the Apostle Paul, who provides the ultimate blueprint for this. He began as "Saul," a man of high status and many credentials. But after encountering Christ, he began a journey of holy reduction. He went from calling himself the "least of the apostles" to "the least of all the Lord’s people," finally arriving at the "chief of sinners." As Paul became smaller in his own eyes, the grace of God became larger in his life.
When we "reduce" ourselves, we aren't losing our value; we are clearing out the clutter of pride to make room for Divine power. Jesus taught that the "poor in spirit" are blessed because they have reached the end of their own resources. When we are empty of ourselves, we are finally eligible to be filled with Him. Making ourselves small isn't about self-hatred; it’s about right-positioning. It is placing ourselves in the shadow of the Almighty so that His light, not ours, is what the world sees.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: "God creates out of nothing. Therefore, until a man is nothing, God can make nothing out of him." — Martin Luther

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Heavenly Father, I thank You for the beauty of humility. Forgive me for the times I have tried to be big in my own strength. Today, I choose to decrease. I lay down my pride, my need for recognition, and my self-sufficiency. Make me small so that Your name can be made great through me. Teach my heart to be poor in spirit, that I may truly inherit the riches of Your Kingdom. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Don't fear the "shrinking" process. When God makes you small, He is simply preparing you to carry a weight of glory that pride could never support. The smaller you become, the more amazing the things God can do through you.
